page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.t5-c1m2.large is a shared burstable instance based on the KVM hypervisor. It runs on an x86_64 Intel Xeon Platinum 8269CY processor clocked at 2.5 GHz, providing 2 vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with 2 threads per core. System memory is sized at 4.0 GB, allocating 2.0 GB per vCPU. The processor includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 35 MB of shared L3 cache, alongside instruction support for AVX, AVX-512 (F and VNNI), AES, BMI2, and FMA. It does not include bundled local storage or dedicated GPUs, and operates with a 0 Gbps baseline network bandwidth profile and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations position the ecs.t5-c1m2.large primarily in the bottom tiers of computing and memory throughput due to its burstable resource constraints. Single-core compute registered a stress-ng score of 1087.69 and a Geekbench single-core score of 891.0, both falling within bottom percentiles. Multi-core performance is limited by the shared 2 vCPU setup, producing a Geekbench multi-core score of 1562.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 2468.66. Memory operations achieved 16.56 GB/sec for uncached large block reads and 14.15 GB/sec for writes. Application-specific benchmarks reflect these constraints, showing 1.96 million operations per second in Redis SET tests, 2.21 GB/sec in static web serving throughput, and 33.17 tokens per second for small 135M model LLM text generation.

The ecs.t5-c1m2.large provides an economical resource configuration for workloads with low baseline CPU utilization that require modest memory allocations. Because it relies on burstable CPU scheduling and shared hardware, sustained high-load workloads risk CPU throttling. It is best suited for entry-level tasks such as low-traffic web serving, lightweight background processing, small test environments, and non-critical development services.
